cpu_stack.notes: The warm-frame stack includes working_buffer -> Metal buffer creation and bind-group creation; TextureView creation is smaller in this sample. The sampler also includes startup and replay, so stack weights are not causal speedup estimates or whole-run CPU percentages. Its single-process physical footprint has no matched control and is not a memory-saving result.

diagnostics.decision: Investigate per-draw data/coverage buffer acquisition and binding overhead before assuming TextureView reuse is the best third optimization. Do not reinstate withdrawn unit-data sharing or claim a new speedup. Device intervals longer than their enclosing measured frame are untrusted; preserve them without filtering, and resolve timestamp reliability before GPU-stage attribution. Host readback includes GPU waits and is not a separate GPU execution duration. Host medians pool all 303 samples per case; percentages are medians of per-frame ratios, not ratios or sums of stage medians. No isolated-idle, cross-device or RSS claim is made.

diagnostics.configuration: Supplemental timestamp-disabled CPU sampling with the existing frozen GPU-only breadth executable on Apple M3/Metal, release, 640x360 and Arial 2a7b70f9cc41bb6b. Each sampler runs for three seconds at a one-millisecond requested interval. nodes-1k uses 501 benchmark samples to keep the process alive through sampling; layers-wide uses 101. Both use two warmups and one iteration, unchanged 1 GiB/20-billion-work limits, and disable scaling, CPU stages, sequences, micro, cold, video and films. The previous timestamp-disabled nodes-10k CPU stack is reused, not resampled.
diagnostics.verification: Both supplemental reports validate against raw measurements and retain exact GPU PPM bytes and original logical resource metrics from the frozen shared-uniform candidate. Their executable fingerprint matches the three earlier stage runs. Existing same-backend seek replay passes. No rendering implementation, shader, benchmark source or cache limit is changed for this assessment; no build directory is recreated.
diagnostics.stack_method: Parse the sample call graph and select warm record_frame subtrees, then their first encode_texture nodes. Sum the first matching creation nodes per branch so nested API wrappers are not counted twice. These are inclusive stack-sample weights, not API call counts, exact CPU percentages or stage milliseconds. Warmups remain within the recorder subtree; startup and replay outside it are excluded. Sampling changes wall times, so these runs are not causal optimization comparisons. Wider-layer encoding also contains other costs; resource weights do not explain its entire latency.
diagnostics.source_assessment: Binding 10 references shared frame strips/spans/alpha uploaded at most once per frame. Each hardware draw separately uploads its binding-4 operation data, obtains a buffer through working_buffer, encodes one copy when staging is available, creates a source TextureView and creates a bind group. Pool lookup is exact size/usage under a mutex with a linear scan; the idle cap is 512 buffers including staging, at most one quarter of the frame allowance and 64 MiB. Bind groups are not pooled. In serial frame encoding with no concurrent pool replenishment, N distinct simultaneously retained draw-data buffers can consume at most 512 preexisting idle buffers, so at least max(0, N - 512) require fresh allocation; other resources and size mismatches can make this worse. This is a bound, not a measured cache-hit count.
diagnostics.packing_tradeoff: An eligible per-batch aligned data buffer could reduce N buffer acquisitions/leases to one and N staging-copy commands to one without rewriting payload words or shader arithmetic. It still needs N bind groups because the existing static uniform offset differs per draw. Storage binding offsets must satisfy the device alignment and expose the original record size. A direct-coverage descriptor has ten f32 words (40 bytes); for the illustrative case of 10000 such records and 256-byte alignment, separate payloads total 400000 bytes while a tightly tailed aligned buffer spans 2559784 bytes. The additional 2159784 bytes, plus corresponding staging padding, require admission or fallback. Actual per-case payload histograms were not measured. Larger payloads, conditional packets, kernels, binding limits and in-flight isolation must remain valid.
diagnostics.decision: Buffer creation is a defensible first prototype target for node-heavy scenes, with bind-group overhead as a separate second target. Do not simply enlarge the idle object cap or reinstate unit-data deduplication. Test aligned binding-4 aggregation independently before attempting explicit dynamic-offset layouts and per-frame bind-group reuse by source/layout/record-size compatibility. Preserve bounded fallbacks and exact pixels; require an uninstrumented frozen AB/BA comparison before retaining an optimization. Current data establish hotspot evidence, not an isolated timing or physical-memory benefit.
